newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico's new elections chief promises clean vote.
newsitem.headline: Mexico's new elections chief promises clean vote.

text.p: The new chief of Mexico's Federal Electoral Institute (IFE) was sworn in Thursday vowing to carry out clean, legal and transparent elections for congressional races next year, a Mexico City newspaper said.

"In the consolidation of this mechanism, the democratic stability of our country is at stake," said Jose Woldenberg, recently named to his post by Mexico's major political parties that make up the IFE, the newspaper Reforma reported.
The naming of an independent head of the electoral institute is one of the major changes contemplated in a landmark electoral reform that has been promoted by President Ernesto Zedillo.

In the past, Mexico's Interior Minister, appointed by the president, was automatically the president of the IFE, which was a major point of contention for parties opposed to the long-ruling Institutional Revolutionary Party (PRI).

The entire nine-member General Council of the IFE was sworn in Thursday. The General Council will be charged with overseeing the IFE, which will be run on a day-to-day basis by an executive secretary.

Woldenberg announced that Felipe Sols Acero would be his candidate for executive secretary of the IFE. Sols, who has had a prominent role with the IFE since 1990, will hold the executive job for several weeks pending a review of his performance, at which time he could be removed, Reforma said.
Woldenberg also said he would order an audit of the IFE at all its levels in order to assure confidence in the institution.
Virtually all of Mexico's local, state and federal elections bring cries of fraud from the losers. The PRI has been in power for 67 years.
